measured_limits_2026_08_08.note: Empirically measured on our actual key — NOT vendor marketing copy (工部尚书's requirement: don't discover the quota weeks in).
measured_limits_2026_08_08.quota_message: "...to lift the free key rate limit (25 requests per day)"
measured_limits_2026_08_08.burst_ceiling: ~1 request/second. An 8-call unpaced burst alternated OK / throttled (4 of 8 throttled).
measured_limits_2026_08_08.per_call_coverage: TIME_SERIES_DAILY&outputsize=compact returns ~100 trading days INCLUDING the latest close, per symbol, in ONE call.
measured_limits_2026_08_08.budget_fit: Paper book caps at 10 names (10% per symbol) + benchmark => ~11 calls/day for a full daily mark, vs the 25/day cap. Fits with ~2x headroom. If the book or marking frequency grows past ~25 calls/day, switch/添加 vendor before it binds.
measured_limits_2026_08_08.throttle_failure_mode: The throttle reply is HTTP 200 with an 'Information' field and NO price data — i.e. it can masquerade as success. quotes_api raises RateLimited on it (see fail_closed).

fallback_vendors_reachable_2026_08_08.purpose: Pre-verified contingency so a QUOTA_DIVERGENCE alarm (or the 25/day cap binding) is executed as a plan, not improvised. Deliberately NOT registered — no key hoarding; register only when actually switching.

twelvedata.reachability: twelvedata.com/pricing -> HTTP 200; api.twelvedata.com -> HTTP 401 (service up, key required)
twelvedata.free_tier_documented: 8 API credits per minute, 800 credits per day (read from their pricing page 2026-08-08)
twelvedata.fit: 800/day vs ~11 needed; the 8/minute limit implies pacing similar to AV's 1/sec discipline we already implement.

fallback_vendors_reachable_2026_08_08.note: Both are materially more generous than Alpha Vantage's 25/day. Neither has been tested for key rotation — if rotation ability ever becomes a selection criterion, verify it BEFORE migrating (the AV lesson: 're-request' is not necessarily rotation; compare hashes).

fail_closed_contract.throttle: RateLimited raised on the HTTP-200-with-no-data throttle reply — never silently treated as 'price unchanged'.
fail_closed_contract.no_fabrication: get_daily_closes returns a `failed` map for symbols that did not come back — never back-filled, never carried forward from a prior run.
fail_closed_contract.stale_marks: mark_to_market raises StalePriceError if a held symbol has no bar or its newest bar is older than max_staleness_days (default 5). A paper mark is never printed from carried-forward or estimated prices.
fail_closed_contract.source_dates_kept: every bar keeps the vendor's own trade date; retrieved_utc (our clock) is stored separately and is never used as a price date.

calendar_resolution: The observed bar dates ARE the trading calendar (observe-not-predict). This removes the earlier CalendarCoverageError root cause: actual_start is decided by the first real bar. No holiday table, no forward-looking calendar, and no reliance on the in-repo SPY daily series (which 工部尚书 found carries ~31 data holes that were being misread as holidays).

live_verification_2026_08_08.sample_mark: holdings {SPY:10, AAPL:20, MSFT:5} -> market_value 16499.15 as_of 2026-08-07, every position priced at its own source trade date

usage: from qlab.events.datafetch import quotes_api as q; bars, failed = q.get_daily_closes(symbols); mk = q.mark_to_market(holdings, bars)  # requires ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY in env

daily_quota_accounting.status: ENFORCED (工部 08-08 hardening): 25/day is an accounted hard budget, not a doc constant
daily_quota_accounting.why: If the day's quota is silently exhausted, every later call throttles -> mark_to_market refuses -> that day has NO paper mark -> a hole in the NAV series, which is this track's only acceptance evidence and cannot be repaired afterwards (the close is gone; back-filling would be fabricating data).

mechanism.persisted_ledger: one JSONL line per call bucketed by UTC day, default ~/.local/state/qlab/av_quota.jsonl (env QLAB_AV_QUOTA_LEDGER). Resumes across processes/restarts so two runs on one day share a counter instead of each counting from zero.
mechanism.pre_call_check: check() raises QuotaExceeded BEFORE the request is issued — we never wait for the vendor's throttle reply to discover exhaustion.
mechanism.marking_reservation: of the 25/day cap, 15 are ring-fenced for mark-to-market (env QLAB_AV_MARK_RESERVE). Exploration may use at most cap-reserve=10, so 'today's NAV point gets recorded' always outranks any other call.
mechanism.conservative_accounting: a call is recorded as soon as the request leaves the host — a throttled/failed call still consumed an attempt. Under-counting is what would silently blow the budget.
mechanism.batch_precheck: get_daily_closes checks the WHOLE batch up front (require_full_batch=True): if today's budget can't cover every symbol it raises before spending anything, rather than burning quota on a partial mark that mark_to_market would reject anyway.
mechanism.breach_propagates: QuotaExceeded is re-raised out of the fetch loop, never buried in the per-symbol `failed` map (which would read as 'symbol unavailable' and keep burning the remainder).
mechanism.status_line: guard.status() reports used/remaining per purpose for the weekly status update — a tightening quota becomes visible instead of hitting a wall.

daily_quota_accounting.day_bucket: UTC date. The vendor's own reset boundary is not precisely documented; UTC is stable and auditable, and the reserve plus ~2x headroom (~11 marking calls vs 25) absorbs any boundary mismatch. QLAB_AV_DAILY_CAP lowers the cap if the vendor tightens it.
daily_quota_accounting.live_verified_2026_08_08: marking call OK then budget exhausted -> QuotaExceeded raised BEFORE any network I/O; a fresh guard over the same ledger resumed the count instead of resetting to 0. Separately confirmed in the wild: today's real 25-call vendor quota was exhausted during rate-limit measurement, and the module surfaced it as RateLimited (never as silent success) — exactly the scenario this accounting prevents from reaching the NAV series.

key_leak_fix_2026_08_08.finding: Alpha Vantage ECHOES the API key inside its daily-quota notice ('We have detected your API key as XXXX...'). That message flowed into the RateLimited exception, which may be logged, reported, or pasted into a status update — a real leak path.
key_leak_fix_2026_08_08.fix: quotes_api._redact() strips the live key by value and then any AV-shaped key token from every vendor message before it reaches an exception.
key_leak_fix_2026_08_08.verified: against the LIVE throttle reply: key absent from the exception text, '<redacted-api-key>' present. Regression test: test_throttle_message_redacts_the_api_key.

quota_exhaustion_event_2026_08_08.what: The vendor's real 25/day quota was fully consumed on 2026-08-08 during the rate-limit measurement (unpaced burst tests + a 12-call paced test + live verification pulls), i.e. BEFORE the accounting layer existed.
quota_exhaustion_event_2026_08_08.how_it_surfaced: Every subsequent call returned the HTTP-200 throttle notice. quotes_api raised RateLimited on it: no price was returned, no stale price was substituted, and mark_to_market would have refused rather than print a value.
quota_exhaustion_event_2026_08_08.why_recorded: This is the live instance of the failure mode the accounting exists to prevent. It demonstrates two things at once: (a) throttling really does happen on this tier, and (b) when it happens we produce NO paper mark rather than a fabricated one. For anyone auditing the NAV series later, this is stronger evidence than a written assurance.
quota_exhaustion_event_2026_08_08.consequence: No NAV point was due on 2026-08-08 (the paper track had not started), so no hole was created in the evidence series. The first real mark waits for the UTC day rollover.
quota_exhaustion_event_2026_08_08.ledger_reconciliation: The production ledger (~/.local/state/qlab/av_quota.jsonl) was seeded with a single reconciliation entry of n=25 for 2026-08-08, noting that the consumption predates the accounting. Rationale: the ledger must not UNDER-count reality — with it recorded, the guard now refuses further calls today (verified: 'requested 1 call(s) but only 0 left today'), which enforces 工部尚书's boundary of waiting for the UTC rollover instead of burning calls that would fail at the vendor. The 2026-08-09 bucket starts clean at 25.

key_rotation_2026_08_08.ruling: 工部尚书: rotate — once a secret has touched an output channel, treat it as exposed (discipline consistency, not because this key is sensitive).
key_rotation_2026_08_08.result: BLOCKED — Alpha Vantage does not support self-service rotation. Re-requesting a key returns the IDENTICAL key; there is no revoke/reissue control in the free flow.
key_rotation_2026_08_08.evidence: Three distinct submissions from this host all returned the same key (sha256 prefix a6b60cc2): (1) agent@clckkkkk.site (the original address), (2) agent+av2@clckkkkk.site (plus sub-address), (3) quant-agent@clckkkkk.site (distinct local part). Keys appear to be issued per domain/requester rather than per address, so no address under our control yields a fresh credential.
key_rotation_2026_08_08.not_done: No fake rotation was recorded and the env file was NOT rewritten with the same value dressed up as new.
options_for_a_genuinely_fresh_credential: Switch the quote leg to a different vendor (Tiingo / Twelve Data — both verified reachable). This yields a never-exposed credential and abandons the exposed one. Cost: new integration + re-measuring limits; it changes the vendor for a leg already certified complete, so it is 工部尚书's call, not a unilateral change.
Ask Alpha Vantage support to revoke/reissue (human-loop, slow, uncertain).
Accept the documented exposure: the key is free, read-only market data, bound to no account balance, no trading capability and no PII; its entire capability is fetching public prices at 25/day.
key_rotation_2026_08_08.residual_risk: Worst case an outsider with this key consumes our 25/day public-data quota. It cannot trade, move money, or read anything private. The redaction fix removes the recurring leak path (the vendor echoing the key in throttle notices).
key_rotation_2026_08_08.redaction_is_key_agnostic: quotes_api._redact reads ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY at call time, so whenever a rotation does happen the by-value redaction covers the new key automatically with no code change (verified against three synthetic replacement keys); the token-shape rule is a second line of defence.

quota_divergence_alarm.status: ENFORCED (工部 08-08 ruling: accept the documented key exposure, add DETECTION instead of rotation — rotation is unavailable at this vendor)
quota_divergence_alarm.risk_it_addresses: This key's entire capability is 25 public-data calls/day: no account, no funds, no PII, no trading. So the only real risk from the exposure is someone else spending the quota -> we hit RateLimited -> no mark that day -> a hole in the NAV evidence series. Detecting that is worth more here than rotating.
quota_divergence_alarm.rule: Before raising RateLimited, read the local ledger. If the vendor reports DAILY quota exhaustion while our ledger still shows budget remaining, the exception is tagged QUOTA_DIVERGENCE and carries ledger_remaining / vendor_throttled / utc_day.
two_causes_it_catches: the key is being spent by someone else (the exposure risk made observable)

our counter has drifted from the vendor's — e.g. their reset boundary differs from our UTC bucketing, which is undocumented. The alarm turns that unknown into a measured signal rather than a silent mismatch.
quota_divergence_alarm.false_alarm_guard: AV's per-second BURST notice also mentions '25 requests per day', so naive keyword matching would fire the alarm on every unpaced burst. _throttle_kind() classifies burst ('spreading out' / 'per second') vs daily exhaustion; only the daily kind can raise QUOTA_DIVERGENCE. Burst throttles are transient and are reported as '(burst throttle)' with divergence=False.
quota_divergence_alarm.conservative_defaults: Without a guard we make no misuse claim at all (ledger_remaining=None, divergence=False) — we do not assert what we cannot measure. Ledger read failures are swallowed so diagnostics can never mask the throttle itself.
quota_divergence_alarm.still_redacted: the divergence path goes through the same _redact, so the vendor's key echo cannot leak via the alarm.
quota_divergence_alarm.operational_note: If QUOTA_DIVERGENCE fires, treat it as a possible key compromise: switch to a fallback vendor (below) and stop using this key. It is the trigger for the pre-verified contingency, not an occasion to improvise.
quota_divergence_alarm.live_validation_2026_08_08: Validated end-to-end against the REAL vendor, not only in unit tests. Today's vendor-side 25/day was genuinely exhausted, so pointing a FRESH ledger (which believes 25 remain) at the live API reproduces the exact leaked-key signature. Result: divergence=True, ledger_remaining=24, vendor_throttled=True, utc_day=2026-08-08, 'QUOTA_DIVERGENCE' present in the message, and the API key did NOT leak into it. The agreeing case was checked too: with the production ledger (which correctly shows 0 left today) the guard refuses before any network I/O, and a no-guard call reports the live throttle as kind='daily' with divergence=False / ledger_remaining=None — no misuse is claimed where none can be measured.
